heading: Chap. vii.—An exhortation to repentance.
paragraphs:
These things, beloved, we write unto you, not merely to
admonish you of your duty, but also to remind ourselves.
For we are struggling on the same arena, and the same conflict
is assigned to both of us. Wherefore let us give up
vain and fruitless cares, and approach to the glorious and
venerable rule of our holy calling. Let us attend to what is
good, pleasing, and acceptable in the sight of Him who
formed us. Let us look stedfastly to the blood of Christ,
and see how precious that blood is to God,[33] which, having been
shed for our salvation, has set the grace of repentance before
the whole world. Let us turn to every age that has passed,
and learn that, from generation to generation, the Lord has
granted a place of repentance to all such as would be converted
unto Him. Noah preached repentance, and as many
as listened to him were saved.[34] Jonah proclaimed destruction
to the Ninevites;[35] but they, repenting of their sins, propitiated
God by prayer, and obtained salvation, although they
were aliens [to the covenant] of God.
